_comment: HNB-identity allowlist for the 3G/Iuh analogue of Signal #5 (5G NG
Setup), Signal #16 (4G S1 Setup), and the 2G Um-side LAI checks -
same pattern, one generation earlier in this lab's history and one
layer more primitive: unlike NGAP/S1AP's numeric gNB-ID/eNB-ID,
HNBAP's id-HNB-Identity IE (TS 25.469 9.2.19) is an OPERATOR-DEFINED
free-text/binary string with NO mandated structure at all - so the
allowlist here matches on the exact identity string plus PLMN, not a
numeric ID space the spec defines.
Every legitimate HNB in this lab must appear here with the EXACT
(PLMN, hnb_identity) it presents in its HNBAP HNB REGISTER REQUEST.
Any HNB REGISTER REQUEST whose tuple is not listed here is flagged as
an HNB-identity allowlist violation (candidate rogue/unauthorised
femtocell) - the direct 3G analogue of a rogue gNB/eNB presenting an
unauthorised identity in this lab's other tiers.
Values below come straight from config/osmocom/osmo-hnodeb.cfg (this
lab's one legitimate HNB) - they are NOT hardcoded into the detector
script, so the same detector works unmodified against a different lab
or a different set of legitimate HNBs: just edit this file.
How to read an HNB's own identity off a real HNB REGISTER REQUEST
using tshark:
- plmn.mcc / plmn.mnc: from the HNB REGISTER REQUEST's id-
PLMNidentity IE, tshark fields e212.mcc / e212.mnc.
- hnb_identity: from tshark field hnbap.hNB_Identity_Info, a hex
octet string that decodes as an ASCII string (this lab's
osmo-hnodeb configures it via the 'identity' VTY/config command,
TS 25.469 9.2.19 imposes no format - it's whatever the vendor/
operator chooses to encode). The detector decodes the hex to text
itself and compares the decoded string, not the raw hex, so this
file stays human-readable.
